subject: Request: continuous VM monitoring attestation + incremental CVE closure log
messages:
From: Omar Ruiz <omar.ruiz@optimabank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: continuous VM monitoring attestation + incremental CVE closure log

Mina,

Thanks again for the quick sync earlier. Optima's audit team is finalizing our SIG/SOC 2 package and asked us to get a short attestation covering your vulnerability management continuous monitoring and an incremental CVE closure log for the last 90 days (and ongoing cadence). Specifically they want: 

- A short attestation letter stating Redwood's scan cadence (authenticated scans and authenticated agent schedule), triage SLA for Critical/High, and exception handling process.
- Export of scan cadence (schedule + last run timestamps) and the incremental CVE closure log with state changes (open -> triaged -> patched/mitigated) for the past 90 days.
- Any attachments or links to the SOC2 evidence portal or evidentiary artifacts (scan exports, patch manifests).

Can you provide the attestation + the incremental export by next week? Audit would like the attestation to include explicit SLA numbers for Critical and High vulnerabilities, and an owner contact if the audit team needs follow-up.

Omar Ruiz
Senior Information Security Manager
Optima Bank
omar.ruiz@optimabank.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Note: If there's a preferred format (CSV vs PDF) for the incremental log, tell us and we'll accept either.
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Omar Ruiz <omar.ruiz@optimabank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: continuous VM monitoring attestation + incremental CVE closure log

Omar — thanks for the details and the clear ask. We can absolutely provide that. I'm attaching a CSV export of our scan cadence and a summarized PDF incremental closure log for the 90-day window. High-level summary below and actions: 

Attachments: vm-cadence-export-20261029.csv, incremental-cve-closure-summary-20261029.pdf

Summary (operational):
- Scan cadence: authenticated full host scans run weekly by default. Critical infrastructure (control plane and runtime islands) have daily authenticated checks for CVE detection and signature updates.
- Triage process: automated triage flags Critical severity immediately to on-call; human triage within 12 hours during business hours.
- SLA commitments (draft): Critical: remediation workflow initiated within 24 hours, remediation target 7 calendar days; High: remediation planning within 3 business days, target 14 calendar days; Medium/Low follow standard backlog with 45/90-day targets respectively.
- Exceptions & compensating controls: where immediate patching is not possible we maintain compensating controls (network ACLs, temporary container image pinning) and an approved exception record with lifecycle and owner.
- Evidence locations: we've included the scan export and a consolidated incremental closure PDF for the 90-day slice. Per your note, CSV is attached for the cadence export. We can also push the full evidence set to a shared Drive link or the SOC2 evidence portal if that works for you.

Next steps: Ben (cc'd) will confirm the final SLA wording and attach the patching schedule.

If Optima wants a signed attestation letter (PDF) we can circulate that after Ben/Kimberly approve the exact SLA language and signatory.

Best,

Mina Haddad
Security Programs Manager
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
Phone: (650) 555-0199

Omar, Mina — adding the concrete SLA language we'll include in the attestation. I attached the quarter's patching schedule for additional context.

Attachment: patching-schedule-2026Q4.xlsx

Proposed SLA language (to be included verbatim in attestation):
- Critical (CVSS >= 9.0 or exploit-known): Initial detection alerting within minutes; remediation workflow started within 24 hours; target for verified remediation or approved compensating control: 7 calendar days.
- High (CVSS 7.0–8.9): Initial triage within 24 hours; remediation plan within 3 business days; target remediation: 14 calendar days.
- Medium/Low: triage and planned remediation per prioritization (target 45/90 calendar days).

Playbook excerpt (short):
- Detection: daily automated scans + continuous OSS vulnerability feeds; critical signatures prioritized.
- Triage: security on-call notified; engineering owner assigned via PagerDuty playbook.
- Remediation: hotfix or configuration mitigation; backport or permanent patch scheduled depending on risk.
- Audit: closure recorded in ticket with evidence (patch diff, CVE reference, verification run).

I'll let Kimberly sign off on the attestation PDF once Mina confirms the attachments are the right exports for Optima's auditors.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer, Vulnerability Ops
ben_carter@redwood.com
